title: Bernoulli example
text: standalone runnable example generates irregular visits baseline time-varying covariate, fits one dataset, saves summaries plots. repository root: Review chain diagnostics reconstructed coefficient curves, random-effect scale, smoothing parameters. tdmm() workflow described Getting Started.
code: library(TDMM) source("examples/bernoulli-getting-started.R") fit <- run_small_bernoulli() summary(fit) plot(fit) plot.trace.tdmm(fit, c("sigma.b", "tau.alpha[1]"))

title: Bernoulli example
text: Bernoulli simulation helper generates one observation per subject random_intercept = FALSE. independent observations, time may represent age, time since event, time relative event. helper defaults 2,500 subjects setting.
code: independent_data <- data.gen.tdmm.bern(random_intercept = FALSE, seed = 27181) fit_independent <- tdmm(independent_data, family = "bernoulli",                         x.var = "x1", random_intercept = FALSE,                         control = tdmm_control(seed = 77181)) summary(fit_independent) plot(fit_independent)

title: Gaussian example
text: Compare reconstructed curves truth() examine pointwise credible bands. Getting Started guide explains scales diagnostics illustrates recovery larger Gaussian dataset.
code: set.seed(27181) truth <- function(t) cbind(beta0 = sin(2*pi*t),                            beta1 = cos(2*pi*t),                            beta2 = 1.5*(t-0.5)) dat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(40), function(i) {   n <- sample(5:8, 1)   time <- sort(runif(n))   baseline <- rnorm(1)   changing <- rnorm(n)   b <- rnorm(1, sd=sqrt(0.5))   beta <- truth(time)   y <- rnorm(n, beta[,1] + baseline*beta[,2] + changing*beta[,3] + b,              sd=sqrt(0.1))   data.frame(id=paste0("person-",i), time=time, y=y,              baseline=baseline, changing=changing) })) library(TDMM) fit <- tdmm(dat, family="gaussian", subject.var="id",             time.var="time", y.var="y",             x.var=c("baseline","changing"), n_basis=8,             control=tdmm_control(chains=3, iterations=4000,               burn_in=1500, thin=2, adapt=2000, seed=77181),             priors=tdmm.priors("gaussian")) summary(fit) plot(fit) plot.trace.tdmm(fit,c("sigma.b","sigma2.e","tau.alpha[1]"))

title: Gaussian example
text: Gaussian simulation helper can also generate one observation per subject. independent-observation study, time may represent age, time since event, time relative event.
code: independent_data <- data.gen.tdmm.gauss(random_intercept = FALSE, seed = 27181) fit_independent <- tdmm(independent_data, family = "gaussian",                         x.var = c("x1", "x2"),                         random_intercept = FALSE,                         control = tdmm_control(seed = 77181)) summary(fit_independent) plot(fit_independent)

title: Getting Started with TDMM
text: Provide one row per observation, columns subject ID, numeric time, response, covariates. order x.var determines coefficient labels: beta1 multiplies first covariate, beta2 second, . baseline repeated within subject changing may vary visit. TDMM handles subject indexing spline construction. Gaussian coefficient curves response scale; Bernoulli coefficients log-odds scale Poisson coefficients log-mean scale. Inspect trace plots, R-hat, effective sample size, credible bands interpretation. random_intercept = TRUE default includes subject-specific random intercept, call . independent observations, use random_intercept = FALSE omit . setting, time may represent age, time since event, time relative event.
code: library(TDMM) fit <- tdmm(long_data, family = "gaussian",             subject.var = "id", time.var = "time", y.var = "y",             x.var = c("baseline", "changing"), n_basis = 8,             control = tdmm_control(chains = 3, iterations = 4000,                                    burn_in = 1500, thin = 2,                                    adapt = 2000, seed = 77181),             priors = tdmm.priors("gaussian")) summary(fit) plot(fit) plot.trace.tdmm(fit, c("sigma.b", "sigma2.e", "tau.alpha[1]"))

title: Getting Started with TDMM
text: figure illustrates recovery simulated data known coefficient functions. Solid lines show posterior means, dashed lines truth, shaded regions pointwise 95% credible bands. Gaussian example gives fitting code. Bernoulli Poisson examples show workflow binary count outcomes.

title: Getting Started with TDMM
text: PBC2 application uses pbc2 dataset JMbayes2: 1,945 observations 312 subjects, 1–16 visits. response log serum bilirubin; predictors baseline treatment indicator longitudinal albumin. Albumin centered overall observation-level mean, 3.3898868894601542 g/dL. Thus intercept represents modeled placebo trajectory albumin level random intercept zero. treatment 95% credible interval includes zero throughout common evaluation grid. albumin coefficient negative, band zero grid. conditional associations, treatment curve establish causal effect. Late follow-sparse, small tail fluctuations read precise clinical changes.

title: Bayesian Time-Dynamic Mixed-Effects Models
text: TDMM provides Bayesian time-dynamic regression models Gaussian, Bernoulli, Poisson outcomes. Regression coefficients vary smoothly time. random_intercept = TRUE (default), subjects may repeated observations, irregular observation times, unequal visit counts, baseline covariates, covariates vary visit. random_intercept = FALSE, model omits subject-specific random intercept independent observations; time may represent age, time since event, time relative event. default spline uses eight cubic B-spline basis functions (polynomial degree 3, spline order 4) second-order coefficient-difference penalty. JAGS performs posterior sampling.

title: Bayesian Time-Dynamic Mixed-Effects Models
text: Install JAGS first, install TDMM R:
code: install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("esrakurum/Bayesian-TDMM") library(TDMM)

title: Bayesian Time-Dynamic Mixed-Effects Models
text: Supply one row per observed visit. baseline constant within subject changing varies visit: Use family = "bernoulli" binary outcomes family = "poisson" counts. See Getting Started data layout, interpretation, diagnostics. Gaussian, Bernoulli, Poisson, PBC2 examples give fuller workflows. vignette source example scripts also available repository.
code: fit <- tdmm(long_data, family = "gaussian",             subject.var = "id", time.var = "time", y.var = "y",             x.var = c("baseline", "changing"), n_basis = 8,             control = tdmm_control(chains = 3, seed = 123)) summary(fit) plot(fit) plot.trace.tdmm(fit, c("sigma.b", "sigma2.e", "tau.alpha[1]"))

title: Fit a Bayesian time-dynamic regression model — tdmm
text: repeated observations, subjects may irregular observation times unequal visit counts; numeric covariates may constant change within subject. independent observations, time may represent age, time since event, time relative event. Coefficient functions use extended uniform B-spline basis second-order coefficient-difference penalty. default cubic eight basis functions. Use tdmm_control(parallel = TRUE, cores = ...) parallel chains. coefficient functions identity, logit, log link scale Gaussian, Bernoulli, Poisson responses, respectively.

title: Fit a Bayesian time-dynamic regression model — tdmm
text: fitted object class "tdmm" containing posterior samples, reconstructed coefficient functions, input metadata, variance summaries, fitting settings.

title: Fit a Bayesian time-dynamic regression model — tdmm
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Requires JAGS and runs MCMC. set.seed(42) my_long_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(20), function(id) {   time <- sort(runif(5))   baseline <- rnorm(1)   changing <- rnorm(5)   data.frame(id = id, time = time, baseline = baseline,              changing = changing,              y = 0.5 + baseline * sin(2*pi*time) +                  changing * (time - 0.5) + rnorm(5, sd = 0.3)) })) fit <- tdmm(my_long_data, family = "gaussian", subject.var = "id",             time.var = "time", y.var = "y", x.var = c("baseline", "changing"),             control = tdmm_control(seed = 42)) summary(fit) plot(fit) } # }

text: Gamma distributions use shape rate parameterization. response families, smoothing precision Gamma(1, 0.001) prior. title: TDMM 0.3.0
text: tdmm() tdmm.parallel() support models without subject-specific random intercept random_intercept; TRUE remains default. Gaussian, Bernoulli, Poisson simulation helpers generate independent-observation data directly random_intercept = FALSE. Repeated-observation models subject-specific random intercept remain supported.

title: TDMM 0.2.0
text: Fit Gaussian, Bernoulli, Poisson longitudinal outcomes subject-specific irregular observation times, unequal visit counts, baseline covariates, time-varying covariates. Use cubic B-splines (degree 3, order 4) second-order coefficient-difference penalty eight basis functions default. n_basis specifies basis dimension directly; older nknots argument remains supported deprecation warning. Fit serial parallel chains tdmm() structured tdmm_control() tdmm.priors() settings. tdmm.parallel() remains compatibility wrapper. Existing Gaussian Poisson model specifications retained.
